items.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo introduces a session-aware inference system designed to optimize agentic workloads that differ significantly from standard chat interactions. Unlike single-turn chats, agent sessions involve large initial prefills, repeated model calls, and parallel subagents, requiring a unified session-level identifier to manage context efficiently. The system transforms request-level infrastructure into a program-aware one, enabling session-aware routing, shared KV cache indexing, and programmatic cache movement across vLLM and SGLang. Key optimizations include session-aware admission control that applies backpressure at tool boundaries to reduce cache thrashing and a shared-pool indexer that accounts for reusable KV in external stores. Testing on SWE-bench showed a 12-16% throughput improvement over standard KV-routing alone at high concurrency, while maintaining a prefix-cache hit rate above 94.5%. The approach relies on a Session-Prefix Indexer and a proposed KvHint interface to coordinate policy intent from the router with execution in inference engines.
items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Introduces Session-Aware Agentic Inference System

items.summary: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, three safety researchers dismissed by OpenAI, published an open letter denying claims that they mishandled sensitive information or engaged in unauthorized external communications. They argue their termination signals a chilling effect that discourages open dialogue and safety collaboration within the company. While OpenAI stated the firings resulted from a pattern of misconduct violating policies on handling research information, a research leader's memo suggested the decisions were not retaliatory. Wang specifically addressed an incident involving accidental access to an executive's email, which she claimed was not hidden. The researchers urge OpenAI to maintain an open culture and support third-party auditors, warning that fear among safety experts could compromise the safe development of AI.
items.title: Fired OpenAI Researchers Deny Misconduct and Warn of Cultural Chilling Effect

items.summary: Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of fraud and replacing American workers with foreign labor through the H1b visa program. Consequently, the White House blocked Microsoft from using the program permanently. Microsoft stated that most filings were for existing employees paid equally to locals. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling halted new applications for the company.
items.title: White House Bars Microsoft From Hiring Foreign Workers

items.summary: Sixteen-year-old Bryce Vincent Gowryluk became the first hiker believed lost due to AI directions when he followed incorrect routes from Claude in British Columbia. The teen required a helicopter rescue after reaching a steep headwall. Search manager Paul Markey warned that artificial intelligence lacks spatial awareness and hikers should question proposed directions before relying on them for navigation.
items.title: Teen Relies on AI for Mountain Route and Requires Rescue

items.summary: OpenAI reportedly told investors its annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, a reduction of roughly $20 billion from earlier reports of nearly $70 billion. The Financial Times notes the previous figure stemmed from investor comparisons with Anthropic. OpenAI's IPO is now delayed until early 2027, and the company raised $122 billion in a March round despite spending significantly more than its leaked 2025 financials suggest.
items.title: OpenAI Revenue Reportedly Falls Short of $70 Billion Projection

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Microsoft is changing its Microsoft 365 Family, Premium, and Pro subscriptions to replace individual storage allowances with a shared pool. Under the new structure, Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans will offer a total of 2 TB of shared storage, down from the previous 6 TB available across five slots. Microsoft 365 Pro will receive 5 TB. Subscribers exceeding these limits may face higher costs, as additional storage costs $10 per month. The changes, described as a form of 'shrinkflation,' are scheduled to begin for new subscriptions on Oct. 8, 2026, and for existing subscribers at their next renewal on or after May 2, 2027. Microsoft states the move provides more flexibility with AI and cloud storage benefits.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Plans to Reduce Shared Storage and AI Credits

items.summary: Sun-ha Hong argues that technology hype systematically wastes societal resources by recycling failed innovations and inflating expectations. Citing examples like the Metaverse and Google Glass, the author contends that this cycle extracts short-term profit while leaving behind invisible costs and burdens. Hong suggests that hype institutionalizes a sense of inevitability around Silicon Valley visions, preventing critical questions about future societal structures. The article posits that this mechanism siphons opportunity costs at a planetary level, hindering genuine progress and alternative possibilities.
items.title: Tech Hype Cannibalizes Future Opportunities Through Systematic Waste

items.summary: City Developments Limited (CDL) has adopted the Electronic Deferred Payment Plus (EDP+) system to replace physical cheques in property transactions. This move aligns with a broader industry shift, as Singaporean banks will stop processing corporate cheques from January 1, 2027. CDL, which began its digital payment journey in 2018, now uses EDP+ to ensure immediate fund deduction, reducing the risk of insufficient funds and streamlining reconciliation. Chia Ngiang Hong, CDL's group general manager, notes that the system enhances payment tracking and supports the company's sustainability goals by reducing reliance on paper-based processes.
items.title: City Developments Limited Switches to EDP+ as Singapore Bans Corporate Cheques

items.summary: Three Singaporean SMEs are transforming decades of operational expertise into new revenue streams through AI and digital tools. Innoflex developed AI assistants to manage maintenance, while Transcend Aero Services converted its aircraft valuation model into a scalable digital capability. Inter-Lab Products is preparing to replicate its hygiene service model in overseas markets. Supported by Enterprise Singapore and SME Centres, these firms utilized business advisors to break down complex digital projects and systematically plan international expansion. The initiative helps small businesses avoid costly mistakes and turn internal knowledge into sellable solutions.
items.title: Singapore SMEs Turn Expertise into AI Tools and Regional Growth

items.summary: The NVIDIA KGMON team placed second in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents competition by developing a system designed to build reliable data analytics agents. The competition required agents to answer natural-language questions using heterogeneous data sources while operating within a small, fixed LLM. The team's approach focused on constraining the action space and making every attempt inspectable. By normalizing data access, limiting tools, and implementing trace inspection, the system reduced failures and improved reliability. The authors note that while the exact solution was shaped by the specific benchmark, the broader principles of building a robust harness around a model can apply to many agent systems.
items.title: NVIDIA KGMON Team Wins KDD Cup with Reliable Agent Harness

items.summary: Airtel Money is listing on the London Stock Exchange, highlighting the growth of mobile money in Africa. While digital payments can help governments collect taxes, the article warns that without clear data protection rules, these systems risk alienating citizens. Drawing lessons from Australia's Robodebt scandal, the author argues that governments must establish guardrails, consult taxpayers, and ensure human oversight in automated decisions. Without embedding trust and accountability, digital tax systems could damage a government's ability to levy taxes effectively.
items.title: Data Protection Needed for African Digital Tax Systems

items.summary: IDC Frontier disclosed that a ransomware attack disrupted its IDCF Cloud service, causing an outage in East Japan Region 1. The attack, which began on October 7, affected 495 companies and local governments. IDC Frontier is investigating the scope of the impact and working to secure other regions. Separately, Nissui Corporation reported a system outage at a third-party data center, though it is unclear if this is connected to the IDCF Cloud attack.
items.title: Ransomware Attack Disrupts Japanese Cloud Service Used by Government Clients

items.summary: Constellation Energy announced a partnership with Google to add 890 megawatts of generating capacity across 11 existing nuclear plants in the PJM Interconnection. The 20-year deal involves upgrading nonnuclear infrastructure to boost output without building new reactors, with a budget topping $4.3 billion. Constellation expects to complete the first uprate by 2028 and the entire batch in the early 2030s. While uprates offer a cost-effective way to add reliable capacity, analysts note that meeting the Trump administration's goal of 5 gigawatts of new nuclear capacity by 2029 will likely require new reactor construction as well.
items.title: Constellation and Google Partner for Nuclear Uprates to Boost Clean Power

items.summary: Kinder Morgan lifted a force majeure on its Tennessee Gas Pipeline after repairs restored natural gas deliveries to Mexico. The outage, which began on October 5, isolated sections including the Rio Bravo and Cenagas meters. While the interruption was brief, Mexico's limited gas reserves and lack of large-scale underground storage highlight its heavy dependence on continuous pipeline deliveries from the United States.
items.title: Kinder Morgan Restores U.S.-Mexico Gas Flows After Pipeline Outage

items.summary: A new Senate bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, seeks to accelerate clean energy development by streamlining permitting and expanding transmission infrastructure. Proponents argue that building renewable capacity is essential to replacing fossil fuels, even if some fossil fuel projects proceed. However, the legislation has fractured the climate movement, with environmental groups criticizing potential rollbacks to protections for tribal nations, endangered species, and marginalized communities. The bill faces an uncertain future in Congress, requiring Republican support to pass major transmission reforms. While some major green organizations remain skeptical, others have expressed support, reflecting a shifting strategy among climate advocates to prioritize clean energy deployment over blocking fossil fuel projects.
items.title: Bipartisan Bill Aims to Accelerate Clean Energy Despite Climate Movement Fracture

items.summary: Rivian announced a 2026 Halloween update featuring a Ghostbusters theme for its vehicles. The update, scheduled for release in October, includes cosmetic interface changes, new light sequences, and a themed voice assistant. A physical Ecto-R1 was created by modifying an R1S, featuring Bill Murray in a promotional video. The features are available on specific software versions for the R1 and R2 models.
items.title: Rivian Launches Ghostbusters-Themed Halloween Update for 2026

items.summary: On October 08, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced enforcement action against American Express Company. The action addresses the firm's failure to sufficiently detect and report suspicious activity related to money laundering. The Board also identified significant deficiencies in the implementation of American Express Company's enterprise-wide anti-money laundering program, particularly at its subsidiary national bank. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has issued a separate enforcement action against the bank.
items.title: Federal Reserve Board Announces Enforcement Action Against American Express

items.summary: More than 120 US lawmakers raised concerns on Thursday regarding Alphabet's Google unit acquiring Spirit Airlines' internal data for $10 million to train artificial intelligence systems. Led by Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Steven Horsford, the lawmakers noted the sale includes 100 million emails and 500 million Microsoft Teams messages. They requested the company exclude employee information from the transaction to the greatest extent possible.
items.title: Lawmakers Oppose Google Acquisition of Spirit Airlines Data for AI Training

items.summary: Apple appointed Steve Smith as head of mergers and acquisitions and moved Adrian Perica to lead its services division, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Thursday. Perica, a 17-year veteran, will oversee iCloud, Fitness+, and News. Eddy Cue, services chief, stated in the memo that the move allows for greater focus on services leadership. Apple did not immediately comment on the shift under new CEO John Ternus.
items.title: Apple Appoints Steve Smith as M&A Chief and Moves Adrian Perica to Services

items.summary: The White House announced that President Donald Trump will present the nation's highest honours for scientific and technological achievement. Recipients include technology industry leaders Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Michael Dell, who are set to receive the National Medal of Science and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
items.title: Trump to honour Musk and Huang with top US science medals

items.summary: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification program, accusing the company of abusing H-1B visas to replace American workers. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the action alongside suspensions for Adobe and several IT firms. Vice President JD Vance criticized Microsoft for cutting 6,000 American jobs while securing thousands of visas, though Microsoft disputes the characterization of its workforce composition.
items.title: Trump Administration Suspends Microsoft from Green Card Program Over Visa Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic published an updated usage policy effective November 12 that prohibits sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward its Claude AI models. The policy also clarifies restrictions on election interference, weapons development, and surveillance. It targets extreme scenarios of cruelty while allowing ordinary frustration or critical feedback. Enforcement will primarily involve terminating conversations with abusive users.
items.title: Anthropic Updates Policy to Ban Abusive AI Use

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services hired 4,258 employees on a net basis in the September 2026 quarter, according to its quarterly fact sheet. This marks the third consecutive quarter of net headcount growth for the company. The final headcount stood at 598,056. Additionally, TCS added around 9,279 employees in Q1 FY27, bringing total net headcount additions for the first half of the fiscal year to 13,537.
items.title: TCS Reports Third Consecutive Quarter of Net Headcount Growth

items.summary: Continental, a Washington law firm with ties to Donald Trump, arranged a trip to Bosnia and Herzegovina for two of his political advisers, according to three sources. The firm received $35,000 monthly from Republika Srpska to organize meetings there. While Trump expressed annoyance about the trip, he did not criticize it harshly. The advisers focused on election integrity rather than political strategy.
items.title: Trump-Tied Firm Organized Balkans Trip for Advisers Amid Criticism

items.summary: Alibaba filed a lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Defense, challenging its classification as a Chinese military affiliate under Section 1260H. The Pentagon listed Alibaba alongside Baidu and Tencent, citing alleged ties to China's state-directed military-civil fusion strategy and indirect affiliation with state-owned entities. Alibaba denies these claims, arguing the listing lacks factual or legal basis and violates its constitutional rights. The DoD submitted public records suggesting Alibaba's compliance with Chinese censorship laws and investments in strategic sectors like space and data centers indicate alignment with Chinese government policies. Alibaba maintains its operations serve commercial and consumer markets, governed by an independent board.
items.title: Alibaba Sues Pentagon Over Military Affiliate Classification

items.summary: A study analyzing 50 African countries finds counterfeit seeds pose a severe risk to farmers by mimicking high-quality varieties. Researchers note that because planting occurs once a season, failure to germinate can destroy an entire harvest. Experts recommend routine surveillance, public awareness programs, and clear penalties to close the gap between policy and implementation.
items.title: Study Warns Counterfeit Seeds Threaten African Crops and Climate Resilience

items.summary: Concerns regarding two unlisted AI companies, Open AI and Firmus, are affecting Wall Street and the ASX. Firmus, an Australian AI factory preparing for an IPO, faces uncertainty after investment banks stopped taking bids. Fund manager Jun Bei Liu notes the listing may not proceed on October 23, citing high financial demands and a lack of proven technology.
items.title: AI firm Firmus faces IPO uncertainty as Wall Street and ASX markets react

items.summary: The peak body for online gambling companies has criticized a proposed bill in the Northern Territory parliament that would mandate deposit caps and ban inducements for major online bookmakers. If passed, the legislation would affect 50 online bookmakers licensed in the NT and their customers nationwide. The bill is scheduled to be introduced to the NT parliament next Wednesday.
items.title: Gambling Lobby Opposes New Deposit Cap and Inducement Ban Bill

items.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln returned to San Diego after more than 10 months at sea, including a record 265 consecutive days. Secretary Pete Hegseth visited the carrier to award the Presidential Unit Citation, rejecting claims of dysfunction. The Navy acknowledged issues like reduced meal options and noted eight suicide attempts among 6,000 personnel, though experts deemed the figure low for the deployment duration.
items.title: USS Abraham Lincoln Returns to San Diego After Record Deployment Amid Crew Concerns

items.summary: A report examines Europe's exposure to spillover from the Ukraine war, citing three Turkish-owned cargo ships hit by suspected Russian drones in EU waters. One vessel, the Alfa Watan, sank off Bulgaria, leaving ten crew members missing. The article questions whether the threat is exaggerated, particularly ahead of elections in Spain, France, and Italy, while noting ongoing Russian attacks on tankers in the Black Sea.
items.title: Europe faces potential spillover from Ukraine war as Russian drones hit cargo ships

items.summary: Protests and anger have grown across Spain following the death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal after her eviction. Her removal from a home of seven decades became the cause celebre of Spain's housing crisis, according to reports from Madrid.
items.title: Spain mourns Maricarmen Abascal, whose eviction sparked housing protests

items.summary: A recent survey led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation and the University of Exeter discovered approximately 180,000 Aldabra giant tortoises on Aldabra Atoll. This figure, based on five years of data, exceeds previous estimates and marks a significant conservation success. However, researchers warn that climate change and invasive species remain threats requiring continued vigilance.
items.title: Survey Reveals Thriving Population of 180,000 Giant Tortoises in Seychelles

items.summary: Thousands gathered at a San Diego naval base to welcome the USS Abraham Lincoln after its 321-day deployment, a record 264 consecutive days at sea. The carrier was diverted to the Middle East due to the US and Israel's conflict with Iran, extending the mission for roughly 5,000 sailors. Reports of hazardous conditions, including food shortages and suicide attempts, sparked political debate. While families celebrated the return, some expressed mixed emotions over missed milestones. The experience shifted some relatives' political views on the president, highlighting the human cost of extended military operations.
items.title: USS Lincoln Sailors Return After Record Deployment Amid Controversy

items.summary: A data centre operated by Russian technology giant Yandex caught fire in the western Ryazan region after what the company said was a Ukrainian drone attack. The facility was taken offline, with Yandex warning that some services could be unavailable. Ukraine also claimed to have struck a major oil refinery in Russia, but the claim could not be independently verified.
items.title: Yandex Data Centre Fire Attributed to Ukrainian Drone Strike

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue fell $20 billion below expectations, contributing to a 1.9% drop in the Nasdaq 100 and a 0.9% decline in the S&P 500. Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.3%, and the Cboe Volatility Index climbed above 16 as investors reacted to energy supply risks and hawkish Federal Reserve comments.
items.title: OpenAI Revenue Drop and Market Volatility

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised interest rates by 25 bps to combat rising inflation, projecting retail inflation at 4.9% in Q2. The central bank shifted its stance to 'calibrated tightening,' signaling a commitment to control inflation despite supply-side drivers like global oil prices and a deficient monsoon. The RBI also revised its 2026-27 GDP growth forecast upward to 7.1%.
items.title: RBI Hikes Rates Amid Rising Inflation and Oil Prices

items.summary: Bankers warn that high hedging costs from RBI swap premiums could discourage foreign investors and pressure the rupee. Kunal Sodhani notes that rising premiums reduce rupee asset attractiveness. A senior official adds that while overseas rates are around 5.50%, adding 3.25% in hedging costs pushes total expenses beyond 9%, making local borrowing at 7.75% a cheaper alternative for companies seeking dollars.
items.title: RBI Swap Premiums May Discourage Foreign Investment

items.summary: The US government suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program following an investigation led by Vice President JD Vance. Officials accused the company of abusing the system by replacing American workers with foreign hires. Microsoft pushed back, stating most H-1B filings were for existing employees. The suspension remains indefinite until the probe concludes.
items.title: US Suspends Microsoft from Green Card Program Over Alleged Abuse

items.summary: A filing by the US Office of Government Ethics details 517 transactions by Donald Trump, including stakes worth at least $1 million in Comcast, Netflix, and others. His largest August purchase was Meta stock valued between $5 million and $25 million. The Trump Organisation states independent institutions manage these holdings without Trump's involvement.
items.title: Trump Discloses Major Stock Purchases in Tech and Energy Firms

items.summary: Rahul Gandhi supported Elon Musk's claims regarding Starlink's delayed launch in India, stating, "Wait till you discover the other guy." The Ministry of Communications refuted allegations of unfair treatment, asserting all satellite firms are at a similar regulatory stage. Musk alleged oligarchs block the company, while Starlink's VP noted investments in 20 gateway sites and local data security.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Elon Musk in Starlink India row

items.summary: On the same day Vice President JD Vance criticized Microsoft for using foreign workers, President Donald Trump prepared to honor CEO Satya Nadella with top technology awards. Vance stated the administration supports Microsoft but will deny permanent residency applications until the company prioritizes hiring American workers. The announcement highlights a contrast between honoring leadership and enforcing stricter immigration policies.
items.title: Trump Honors Nadella While Vance Criticizes Microsoft Hiring

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India issued notices to Dr Reddy's, Nestle Health Science, and e-commerce platforms for selling the 'CELEVIDA GLP' supplement with misleading health claims. The regulator stated that advertisements implying the product supports muscle preservation during GLP-1 therapies could mislead consumers. Amazon confirmed the product is no longer available on its marketplace, while other companies have not yet responded.
items.title: FSSAI Issues Notices to Companies Over Misleading Protein Supplement Claims

items.summary: Elon Musk questioned why Starlink lacks an Indian licence despite complying with local laws for five years and operating in 165 other countries. He alleged that oligarchs were blocking the service. In response, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi cryptically replied, "Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy." The Indian government rejected Musk's claims as baseless, stating its regulatory framework is fair and non-discriminatory. While Starlink holds a GMPCS licence, it awaits security clearance and spectrum assignment before commercial operations can begin. The ministry noted that Starlink, along with Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications, is currently undergoing security assessments.
items.title: Musk Questions Starlink India Licence Delay Amid Regulatory Scrutiny

items.summary: Infosys and Wipro ADRs fell nearly 3% following TCS's strong quarterly earnings and a US suspension of several tech firms from the PERM green card programme. US Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abuse, while Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling listed Infosys, Wipro, and others among suspended companies. The move adds to investor concerns regarding foreign-worker scrutiny and US market reliance.
items.title: Infosys and Wipro stocks fell after TCS earnings and US immigration crackdown

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 0.25 per cent, prompting volatility in debt mutual funds as bond prices fell. Experts note that while short-term NAVs may decline, the shift to a 'calibrated tightening' stance suggests the rate cycle is not yet peaked. Investors are advised to focus on high-quality short- and medium-duration funds to navigate the higher borrowing costs and potential yield increases.
items.title: RBI Rate Hike Volatilizes Debt Mutual Funds Amid Tightening Cycle

items.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier requested a court order requiring Meta to remove users under 14 from Facebook and Instagram, limit teen usage to two hours daily, and disable autoplay features. Uthmeier pursued this action separately from a broader settlement reached by Meta with 48 other states. Meta's spokesperson criticized the lawsuit as meritless, arguing resources should target other platforms like YouTube and TikTok instead.
items.title: Florida Sues Meta Over Teen Safety on Social Platforms

items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court ordered the revival of Ibra Khan's passport, allowing her to complete her MBBS in Iran. Authorities had impounded it based on a 1997 CID report against her father, citing security apprehensions despite Khan being born in 2005. The court dismissed concerns about her joining anti-India forces and directed authorities to impose conditions if necessary.
items.title: Jammu and Kashmir High Court Orders Passport Revival for Student in Iran

items.summary: Vote counting for five Assembly constituencies and one Lok Sabha seat is scheduled for Friday. The counting begins at 8 am, with results expected throughout the day. The contests include seats in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry, as well as Nagaon in Assam. Updates will be provided by the Election Commission of India and The Times of India.
items.title: Vote Counting Scheduled for Friday in Five Assembly Seats and One Lok Sabha Seat

items.summary: The Madras High Court directed police to permit the first death anniversary observance of P. Nagendran, the prime accused in the 2024 murder of BSP leader K. Armstrong. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan quashed a police denial, allowing the event at the family's Vyasarpadi residence with restrictions on participants, timing, and conduct. The court noted the deceased's status while affirming the family's right to customary observances.
items.title: Madras High Court Allows Death Anniversary Observance for Prime Accused

items.summary: Palm oil-producing countries aim to strengthen ties with India, the world's largest vegetable oil importer. This focus was highlighted at GLOBOIL India in Mumbai, where industry leaders discussed supply security, sustainability, and the impact of biofuel policies. Companies like AWL Agri Business and Patanjali Foods received trade awards for their imports. Producers view India as a strategically important market, while India seeks diversification and supply security beyond short-term price considerations.
items.title: Palm Oil Producers Seek Closer Ties With India Amid Growing Demand

items.summary: Sakinaka police in Mumbai filed an FIR against 42-year-old businessman Sarfraj Kadari for allowing his 15-year-old son to ride a motorcycle without a licence. Police spotted the boy riding rashly at 11.55 am on Saki Vihar Road. Kadari was booked under the Motor Vehicles Act. This follows a similar case in Bandra where a father was booked for allowing his 17-year-old son to ride a scooter.
items.title: Mumbai Police Book Father for Allowing Minor to Ride Motorcycle

items.summary: The Mumbai Bench of the National Company Law Tribunal approved 35 resolution plans worth over Rs 4,189 crore in Q2 FY2026-27, making it the top-performing bench in India. Nationally, 107 plans involving Rs 11,071.17 crore were approved, marking the highest quarterly disposal since the tribunal's inception. The Mumbai Bench accounted for 38% of the total approved value. The tribunal cited institutional constraints, including vacancies and infrastructure challenges, as ongoing issues.
items.title: Mumbai NCLT Bench Leads India in Resolution Plan Approvals

items.summary: MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal is named in an FIR alleging an attempt to delete a living voter's name. Abdul Razak claims a fake death certificate was submitted on Yatnal's letterhead to the Vijayapura City Corporation Commissioner. Three other FIRs in the district involve similar allegations regarding the deletion of voters' names during the SIR exercise, raising concerns about community differences and the inclusion of deceased persons on electoral rolls.
items.title: MLA Yatnal Named in FIR Over Alleged Voter Name Deletion Bid

items.summary: Citizens in New Delhi face a dilemma regarding an October 10 protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Police have invoked Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita to ban gatherings, warning that participation could disrupt law and order. While some residents and shopkeepers fear detention and refuse to support the protest, youth organizations and residents' welfare groups continue door-to-door mobilization efforts. These groups argue that affected working-class individuals must exercise their right to protest despite police restrictions and potential transport disruptions.
items.title: Citizens Divided Over October 10 Protest Calls Amid Police Warnings

items.summary: Former Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida told The Hindu that Japan faces its most severe security environment since World War II. He cited China's activities in the South China Sea as heightening regional tensions. Kishida stated Japan is strengthening its defense capabilities while maintaining the U.S. alliance and expanding cooperation with partners in the Indo-Pacific, including India.
items.title: Former Japanese PM Kishida Warns of Severe Security Environment
